## 2. Today's concepts

### A. The three names

| | what it is |
|---|---|
| **JPA** (Jakarta Persistence API) | a *specification* (interfaces + annotations) for mapping Java objects ↔ relational tables — "ORM" |
| **Hibernate** | the most common *implementation* of JPA; Spring Boot uses it by default |
| **Spring Data JPA** | Spring layer on top: you declare a repository *interface*, Spring generates the implementation at runtime |

Same pattern as always: spec/interface vs implementation.

### B. Entity = a class mapped to a table

```java
import jakarta.persistence.*;

@Entity                                       // this class is a table row type
@Table(name = "todos")                        // optional; default table name = class name
public class Todo {

    @Id                                       // primary key
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)   // DB auto-increments it
    private Long id;

    @Column(nullable = false)                 // optional column tweaks
    private String title;

    private boolean done;

    protected Todo() {}                       // JPA REQUIRES a no-arg constructor (can be protected)

    public Todo(String title) { this.title = title; }

    // getters/setters …  (id has a getter, usually no setter)
}
```

Rules of thumb:
- Every entity needs `@Id`. `@GeneratedValue` means *don't set it yourself*; it's `null` until saved.
- Use wrapper `Long`, not `long`, for the id so "unsaved" can be `null`.
- Each field → a column by default; `@Transient` to exclude one.
- `equals/hashCode` on entities is subtle (id is null before save) — for this course, id-based equality after save is fine.

### C. `JpaRepository` — the repository you don't write

```java
public interface TodoRepository extends JpaRepository<Todo, Long> {   // <entity type, id type>
    List<Todo> findByDone(boolean done);                 // derived query — Spring writes the SQL from the NAME
    List<Todo> findByTitleContainingIgnoreCase(String part);
    long countByDone(boolean done);
}
```

Free methods from `JpaRepository`:

| method | does |
|---|---|
| `save(entity)` | INSERT if id null, otherwise UPDATE; **returns the saved entity (with id)** |
| `findById(id)` | returns `Optional<Todo>` — not the entity, not null |
| `findAll()` | `List<Todo>` |
| `deleteById(id)`, `delete(entity)` | |
| `existsById(id)`, `count()` | |

Derived query naming: `findBy` + `FieldName` [+ `And`/`Or` + …] [+ `OrderByFieldAsc`]. Keywords: `Containing`, `StartingWith`, `LessThan`, `Between`, `IgnoreCase`, `In`. Field names must match the entity's fields exactly (compile fine, fail at startup if wrong).

### D. `Optional<T>` — brief

```java
Todo t = repo.findById(id).orElseThrow();                       // NoSuchElementException if absent
Todo t2 = repo.findById(id).orElse(null);
repo.findById(id).ifPresent(x -> x.setDone(true));
```
Optional is a box that may be empty — forces you to handle "not found" instead of NPE-ing.

### E. Wiring it in

```java
@Service
public class TodoService {
    private final TodoRepository repo;                            // inject the INTERFACE; Spring supplies a proxy bean
    public TodoService(TodoRepository repo) { this.repo = repo; }

    public Todo add(String title) { return repo.save(new Todo(title)); }
    public List<Todo> findAll()   { return repo.findAll(); }
    public void toggle(Long id) {
        Todo t = repo.findById(id).orElseThrow();
        t.setDone(!t.isDone());
        repo.save(t);
    }
}
```

Config (`application.properties`) for the usual in-class setup with **H2** in-memory DB:
```
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:todos
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update      # create/alter tables from entities (dev only)
spring.h2.console.enabled=true            # browse at /h2-console
spring.jpa.show-sql=true                  # see generated SQL in the log
```
Dependencies in `pom.xml`: `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa` + `h2` (runtime).

### F. Mental model

`Todo` object ⇄ row in `todos` table. `save` = INSERT/UPDATE, `findAll` = `SELECT *`, `deleteById` = `DELETE WHERE id=?`. Hibernate writes the SQL; you write Java.

## 3. Self-check (~5 min)

1. What's wrong: `@Entity class Todo { private Long id; ... }`
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>Missing <code>@Id</code> (and probably a no-arg constructor).</details>
2. Name the method Spring generates for `List<Todo> findByDoneAndTitleStartingWith(boolean d, String p)` — what SQL?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary><code>SELECT … FROM todos WHERE done = ? AND title LIKE 'p%'</code>.</details>
3. What does `findById` return, and why?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary><code>Optional&lt;Todo&gt;</code> — so callers must handle absence explicitly.</details>
4. `Todo t = new Todo("x"); repo.save(t); System.out.println(t.getId());` — is the id set on `t`, or only on the return value?
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>With IDENTITY generation Hibernate sets it on the same instance, but the safe habit is to use the returned entity: <code>t = repo.save(t)</code>.</details>
5. JPA vs Hibernate vs Spring Data JPA — one word each.
   <details><summary>Answer</summary>Specification / implementation / Spring's repository layer.</details>
